text:
lina: FYI nightly-gpu shards 3/5 failing on quantized_attention_test — OOM + illegal memory access on a100-32g. Anyone seen this on main? Logs look noisy.

raj: Can you paste the shard logs/artifacts link?

lina: job: https://ci.redwood.internal/jenkins/job/nightly-gpu/3425/artifacts/ — main relevant snippet below:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
[CUDA] driver: 535.54.10, cuda runtime: 12.4
GPU: A100-SXM4-40GB
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../quant/attention.py", line 412, in forward
    out = cuda_kernel(... )
CUDAError: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

sasha: We rolled node pool image to cuda12.4 yesterday. Some runners still on older driver bits — mismatch can cause kernel launch faults.

yun: Lina, can you try with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and repro `pytest tests/quant -k attention -q`? Short run should show deterministic crash.

lina: Rerunning with C_LB=1 now, will paste output when done.

infra-bot: Triggered rerun: nightly-gpu #3425 shard 3 by @lina — queued on pool a100-2.

lina: New run shows cudnn error then OOM: 
```
cuDNN error: CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR at /build/cudnn/ops/convolution.cu:231
Workspace malloc failed: requested 268435456 bytes, available 134217728
RuntimeError: out of memory during cudnnFindConvolutionForwardAlgorithm
```

tanya: That looks like cudnn autotune picked an algo needing large workspace. We added a workspace cap in runtime/config.py on canary only. @raj did that land to nightly?

raj: I merged the cap to canary but not to nightly image yet — forgot to bump build. I'll cut a quick backport patch.

sasha: Temporary mitigation: set `CUDNN_WORKSPACE_LIMIT_BYTES=104857600` on the runner env to avoid huge workspace selection.

yun: If driver/runtime mismatch is the root cause, changing workspace might not help. What driver version are CI nodes running? @infra-bot?

infra-bot: Node metadata for a100-2: driver=535.86.05, cuda-toolkit=12.4, cudnn=8.9.2.

sasha: 535.86 should normally be fine with 12.4, but we've seen edge-case PTX JIT issues that lead to illegal memory access (kernel variant selection). We should compare on h100 to isolate a100-specific problem.

lina: I can request an h100 run but need quota — pinging devops.

devops: Granted 1 h100 trial for 30m to @lina. Use pool `ci-scratch/h100-1`.

lina: Running now on h100. If it passes there, likely a100 driver/kernel path bug.

raj: If h100 passes, open infra ticket with `dmesg`, `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, and `nvidia-bug-report` output from a100 node. Also consider adding a runtime flag to disable cudnn autotune as a fallback.

sasha: :thumbsup: I'll open an infra ticket if h100 is green. If it fails on h100 too, we probably introduced a regression in the attention kernel and will need to bisect commits.

lina: Update: h100 run PASSED. Opening infra ticket #4234 with logs/artifacts + repro command. Marking nightly job as flaky and skipping quantized_attention_test in the next run to avoid noisy alerts.

ci-bot: Label applied: flaky/triaged by @lina.

tanya: Thanks. In the ticket, include the exact repro command, env vars, and suggested mitigations (workspace cap, `CUDNN_WORKSPACE_LIMIT_BYTES`, or `--no-cudnn-autotune`). Also attach `LD_PRELOAD` info if we need to force older libcudnn path.

lina: Will do. Leaving followups in infra ticket. Thanks all for quick responses.
